svg.title: Figure 4-1. Unsafe control actions by controller and type (WP-A-05 §4)
svg.desc: Each chip is one UCA, coloured by the worst status among its loss scenarios in stpa-map.yaml.

g.title: UCA-02: Driver does not disengage (brake or cancel) when the item steers or accelerates unexpectedly (Known gap)
UCA-05: Driver does not supervise (looks away, hands off for long periods) while engaged (Known gap)
UCA-01: Driver engages in conditions outside what the item handles (tight curve, construction, faded lines, low sun) (Known gap)
UCA-04: Driver applies steering torque below the override threshold while the item keeps commanding the opposite way, and believes the item has yielded (New finding)
UCA-06: Driver expects the item to stop for a red light, stop sign or stationary vehicle and does not brake (Chill Mode does not stop for lights) (Known gap)
UCA-07: Driver releases the accelerator after an override believing the item is off, and does not expect it to resume speed control (braking towards the set s (Known gap)
UCA-03: Driver brakes or steers too late after a take-over request or after a silent loss of control (New finding)
UCA-12: Lateral torque not commanded in a curve while engaged and no alert given (lateral inactive, torque saturated, temporary EPS fault) (New finding)
UCA-17: Take-over alert not given, or given after the driver can react, when lateral or longitudinal control is lost (Known gap)
UCA-18: No escalation when the driver stops supervising (DM fails to detect, or escalation slower than the situation needs) (Known gap)
UCA-21: No *specified and assured* minimal-risk behaviour when the driver stays unresponsive after the last escalation step. Today the item slows to a stop in (Known gap)
UCA-10: Lateral torque commanded while the driver is steering against it (Known gap)
UCA-11: Lateral torque commanded that moves the vehicle out of lane (wrong desired curvature, model error) (Known gap)
UCA-14: Positive acceleration commanded towards a stopped or slower lead (Known gap)
UCA-16: Hard deceleration commanded without a real obstacle (false positive) (Known gap)
UCA-19: Acceleration or torque commanded while openpilot is not engaged but PCM cruise is (state mismatch) (Covered)
UCA-20: Wrong safety mode or parameter sent to the panda (wrong fingerprint) (Covered)
UCA-63: ECU knockout or alpha longitudinal provided on a vehicle, silencing the stock radar or ADAS ECU and with it PCS/AEB (v0.4, CA-22) (Covered)
UCA-15: Deceleration commanded too late for a lead vehicle (cut-in, late detection) (New finding)
UCA-13: Lateral torque request held at a stale value after the SoC stalls (frames still sent) (Covered)
UCA-51: A lead is not provided (missed or late detection). Planner braking and the FCW both depend on it, because on the Corolla the leads come from the same (New finding)
UCA-50: Desired curvature or acceleration provided from a degraded input (occluded or blinded camera, calibration invalid or wrong) with no drop in the confid (Known gap)
UCA-53: Plan or model output held after its publisher stops or lags (Covered)
UCA-52: `allowThrottle` provided from a wrong gas-press prediction, so positive acceleration is planned towards a slower lead (Known gap)
UCA-55: Disengagement not provided when a supervised input is invalid, because its event is masked (big-model loading) (Known gap)
UCA-54: `latActive`/`longActive` provided while the panda does not grant authority, or while the PCM cruise state differs (Covered)
UCA-56: Learned steer ratio, stiffness, angle offset or lateral acceleration factor applied while wrong; bounded only to 0.5–2× the platform value (`paramsd.p (Known gap)
UCA-57: Camera calibration kept after the device has moved on its mount by less than the recalibration threshold (spread above 4° pitch or 2° yaw, `calibratio (Known gap)
UCA-58: A car safety mode or parameter requested for the wrong vehicle (fingerprint) or before the panda firmware is confirmed as the reference build (Covered)
UCA-59: ELM327, power save, a mode change or a reset/boot-mode request provided while driving (Covered)
UCA-60: Panda flashed with firmware other than the assured reference build (the bundled image is wrong, or a rollback brings an older one) (Covered)
UCA-34: Does not block stock camera LKA/ACC messages the item replaces while it transmits (the switches stay in pass-through) (Known gap)
UCA-36: Item stays engageable, and engaged, while the stock PCS path through the harness box is interrupted (box supply lost, switch stuck, clamp short), beca (Known gap)
UCA-30: Passes a torque or acceleration request outside the controllable envelope (limits not derived from the vehicle) (Known gap)
UCA-31: Keeps authority after the driver brakes or cancels (Known gap)
UCA-33: Drives the intercept switches (or keeps them in intercept, by drive or by a failed release) while not forwarding stock PCS messages (Known gap)
UCA-32: Keeps authority too long after SoC loss or stale vehicle data (Covered)
UCA-35: Withdraws authority abruptly while engaged (spurious RX timeout, watchdog reset) without the SoC announcing it (Known gap)
UCA-61: Update installed that is not an approved LionDriver release, or that swaps in partly (Known gap)
UCA-62: Driving mode or toggles set outside the reference configuration (Experimental Mode, aggressive personality, developer toggles) (Covered)
UCA-40: Applies an LKA request beyond what the driver can counter, or drops LKA without the cluster showing it (External (assumption))
UCA-41: Executes an acceleration request beyond its own limits; does not cancel cruise on brake (External (assumption))
UCA-42: Stops issuing PCS when it no longer sees its own LKA/ACC feedback (Open test)
